html:
The Popoloca, who call themselves Ngiwa, are an Indigenous people of southern Puebla in Mexico, around the Tehuacán Valley. Their language is one of the Oto-Manguean languages, close to Mazatec, and they should not be confused with the Popoluca of Veracruz, whose name is similar.

The Tehuacán Valley is one of the places where early maize farming was first studied, in caves used for thousands of years. In the 1400s the Popoloca towns of the region were conquered by the Aztec Triple Alliance and paid it tribute. After the Spanish conquest most Popoloca came to speak Spanish; the language is still spoken in a few towns.
